verdict.rationale: Luma's docs list image-to-video as a capability of its current video model and price I2V clips, so animating a still image is first-party. They do not explicitly state that the source image's subject and composition stay intact; that is only implied by the character-reference and keyframe features. One community report of morphing and weak temporal coherence is general, not an I2V counter-example, so it lowers confidence rather than creating a dispute. missing for 10: explicit documentation that I2V preserves subject and composition, I2V-specific controls or limits, independent hands-on corroboration of fidelity to the input image.

support.subject: As a creator, I can animate a still image into motion with the subject and composition preserved

citations.quote: Current video model — text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video with character reference and keyframes
